definition: Dragon Dictation started as speech recognition application for Apple's iOS platforms, including iPhone, iPod Touch and iPad.
details: The app provided automatic speech-to-text capabilities. It was developed by Nuance Communications, and released in December 2009 as a free app. It is now commonly found licensed in vehicle infotainment systems and healthcare equipment. Dragon Dictation speech recognition is based on Dragon NaturallySpeaking speech recognition technology from Nuance Communications. It works online, requiring an Internet connection by the user. Other apps which used the same speech recognition technology include Siri, which Apple acquired in 2010 and is now integrated into iOS. In July 2010, Nuance reported that there had been 3.7 million downloads of their iPhone apps, and Dragon Dictation ranked as the number one business productivity app in Apple's iTunes App Store. Eventually, the software became available for devices running the Android operating system through other Nuance apps like the Swype Keyboard and the Dragon Mobile Assistant. However, in February 2018, Nuance announced a focus on the enterprise market which resulted in them discontinuing these apps.

explainer.lead: Dragon Dictation was Nuance Communications’ speech-to-text app, first released free for Apple’s iOS devices in December 2009. It let people speak instead of type, using Dragon NaturallySpeaking recognition technology over an Internet connection.

tiers.eli5: Dragon Dictation was like having someone type while you talked. You spoke into an iPhone, iPod Touch, or iPad, and the app turned your words into written text. It needed the Internet to do this, much like asking a helper who was not inside the phone.
tiers.practitioner: Dragon Dictation applied Nuance’s online automatic speech recognition to dictation on iOS, with the Internet connection as a hard dependency. Its recognition technology was based on Dragon NaturallySpeaking, while later Android access came through Nuance apps such as Swype Keyboard and Dragon Mobile Assistant. Those consumer apps were discontinued after Nuance announced an enterprise-market focus in February 2018; the technology is also licensed in vehicle infotainment and healthcare equipment.
tiers.paperLevel: Formally, Dragon Dictation implemented automatic speech recognition as f(speech) = text, using recognition technology based on Dragon NaturallySpeaking. The application operated online rather than as an offline recognizer. Its original platform scope was iOS, and no accuracy figures or model architecture are specified.

explainer.example: A user could speak a short message into an iPhone instead of typing it on the keyboard. Dragon Dictation would process the speech online and display the corresponding text.

explainer.intuition: Instead of treating typing as the only way to enter text, Dragon Dictation treated speech as the input. The user supplied spoken words, and Nuance’s recognition technology produced a written version.
howItWorks: The user speaks into a supported device.
The app captures the speech for automatic speech-to-text processing.
Recognition runs online using technology based on Dragon NaturallySpeaking, so an Internet connection is required.
The app provides the recognized words as text.
explainer.whyItMatters: It brought Nuance’s established Dragon recognition technology to mobile dictation as a free app. By July 2010, Nuance reported 3.7 million downloads of its iPhone apps, and Dragon Dictation ranked as the number one business productivity app in Apple’s iTunes App Store.
misconceptions: It did not work entirely offline: an Internet connection was required.
It was not Siri, although Siri used the same speech-recognition technology.
Its later Android presence was through other Nuance apps, not simply the original iOS app.
